context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 15 March 1898], Hotel de Nice, Paris. Three days after Arthur Symons's review of The Ballad of Reading Gaol appeared in Harris's Saturday Review, and a week before the fifth edition. He is grateful, hungry, and out of money for newspapers.
quote:
Hotel de Nice, Rue des Beaux Arts, Paris

My dear Frank, It gave me great pleasure to find that the most sensitive and intellectual appreciation of my poem appeared in your paper. I am greatly touched by Symons’ article; it is most admirably phrased, and its mode of approach is artistic and dignified — a thousand thanks to you, and to him.

When do you arrive?

I have a ‘faim de loup’ for your presence, and for dinner — I am eating the ‘vache enragée’ with a vengeance, which probably accounts for my Greek handwriting having become a scrawl —

I wish you would let me have the Saturday — for the papers are so dear here.

Ever Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 43-44 - one bifolium on paper with a 'Currente Calamo' pen device: image 43 shows sides 4 (left) and 1 (right), image 44 the inner opening, sides 2 and 3. Emphasis: none across the four sides, a null finding. A third treatment of French, on one sheet: '‘faim de loup’' and '‘vache enragée’' are in his own inverted commas and not underlined. So across this correspondence his French is sometimes unmarked (p. 1123), sometimes underlined (pp. 1124-1125, 1131, 1115), and sometimes quoted (here). The volume italicises all three treatments identically, which is why its italic on French carries no information at all. Title: 'the Saturday' is written plain here, without the quotation marks he gave it twice at p. 1042; the volume italicises it in both letters. He was not consistent, and the edition conceals that he was not. Reading: 'Symons'' with his apostrophe after the s; the volume prints 'Symons's'.
